hook.en: Rice, dal, milk and oil all changed price by different amounts. How do we combine four changes into one *index* without weights?

say.en: Rice, dal, milk and oil all changed price by different amounts. How do we combine four changes into one index without weights? In this lesson: Compute the simple aggregative index.
Compute the simple average of price relatives AM and GM.
State the defects of unweighted indices.

body.en: Add the current prices and the base prices of all items and compare the totals: $P_{01} = \frac{\sum p_1}{\sum p_0} \times 100$. It is easy, but items with high prices dominate, and the result changes if a price is quoted per quintal instead of per kg (it fails the unit test).

narration.en: The simple aggregative index is the total of current prices over the total of base prices, times one hundred. Costly items dominate it.
narration.kn: ಸರಳ ಸಮಷ್ಟಿ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ = ಪ್ರಸಕ್ತ ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ ÷ ಆಧಾರ ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ × 100. ದುಬಾರಿ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಾಬಲ್ಯ ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: The simple aggregative index is the total of current prices over the total of base prices, times one hundred. Costly items dominate it. Easy to compute.

say.en: Three items: rice, milk and cloth. Set the current price of rice. The simple aggregative index adds the prices, so quoting rice per quintal instead of per kg changes the index. Indices built from price relatives AM or GM do not change: they pass the unit test.

body.en: First find the price relative $\frac{p_1}{p_0} \times 100$ of each item, then *average* them. Using AM: $P_{01} = \frac{1}{n}\sum \frac{p_1}{p_0} \times 100$. Using GM: $P_{01} = \text{antilog}\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum \log\left(\frac{p_1}{p_0}\times 100\right)\right]$. Relatives are pure numbers, so this index is not affected by units.

points.en: GM version satisfies the time reversal test
Still gives equal importance to all items

problem.en: Compute (i) the simple aggregative index and (ii) the simple AM and GM of price relatives. Items Rice, Dal, Milk, Oil; p₀ = 40, 80, 20, 100; p₁ = 60, 100, 30, 120 (₹).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Compute (i) the simple aggregative index and (ii) the simple AM and GM of price relatives. Items Rice, Dal, Milk, Oil; p₀ = 40, 80, 20, 100; p₁ = 60, 100, 30, 120 (₹).

say.en: Let us work this out together. Compute i the simple aggregative index and ii the simple AM and GM of price relatives. Items Rice, Dal, Milk, Oil; p 0 equals 40, 80, 20, 100; p 1 equals 60, 100, 30, 120 (₹).
Σp 0 equals 240, Σp 1 equals 310; simple aggregative equals 310 over 240 times 100 equals 129.17.
Price relatives: 150, 125, 150, 120.
AM of relatives equals 545 over 4 equals 136.25.
GM equals antilog[Σ log P/4] = antilog2.1321 equals 135.54.
So the answer is 129.17; AM 136.25; GM 135.54.
